en: Going about without sleeping,
From there, Kyrgyz and [?] Kazakh:
Its crescent-shaped ear like a shield,
Its foremost eye like the morning star,
Like a lamb’s tail curled up,
When seen, appearing like this,
Tall, with broad shoulders,
Of medium height, with a stern face,
At the time when stone would burn,
Then a man named Kayyp,
Spoke one word worth ten men’s words,
He spoke stern words to his face,
“If you ask about me,
I myself am of the name Shay,
Of the khoja called Sebet,
The son called Er Jolbors,
Firewood and a crossing [?],
Your people in Kozoy-Joo,
Known as Muslims,
His occupation is worldly trade,
Now before the eyes, now out of sight,
Know it for the sake of your father,
Even if it is a seven-day journey,
If you are wise, understand it,
Born from [?],
Having heard tidings upon tidings,
Climbing across the breadth of the land,
Standing outside and lingering,
Everyone heard of your deeds,
That blooded he-goat [?],
From abundance comes generosity,
Whatever has eyes gnaws at it.
Gnawing at this, it makes it its work,
Let it gnaw however much it thrives,
It does [?] to the four enclosures,
Beginning at the precipice, it takes life,
The blood of us all flows,
Your eye lets this fall to the ground,
In a foreign land it cannot turn aside,
Among foreign people it does no different deed,
Pass from the rich man to true blood,
What sort of man will be strong,
The hardship encountered will be a fire,
Seeing those things,
Did you send it from here to [?],
Without diminishing his people [?],
Did you leave after saddling Burak,
Kenen, who came through the dark night,
Asking my news, his every affair,
Black on the outside, blue at the breast,
There is no hero standing without you,
Train yourself in speech,
Bride, enter among the people,
It is a hero’s deed to wage battle,
Make camp at the Talas citadel,
His mother raced Kozoy’s horse,
Give Kenen the pacing horse,
Saying he should guard the people without losing them,
His anger was like wheat on black earth,
Saying, “Be spent for your people,”
When told to take a cap, he cut off a head,
When told to take boots, his head [?],
Leave that to Kenen,
In awe, defer to him,
It was a land endowed with fortune.
That man’s lineage is from God,
Like the livestock of the abyss,
If you understand, he will act on you quickly,
He will turn what you see into livestock,
If you bring it, he will do it quickly,
Whatever you await, that is the brave man,
That is the unexpectedly formidable man,
Has the scout gone ahead?
Did your mother descend to the place of honor, khan?
The khan has come to Ay-Salam,
Go out once on patrol at night.
My fierce warrior-khan, Tülüş,
My Kara-Kyrgyz, you have your standing,
If you settle after telling Keneş,
He has done the deed he laughed about,
What was lacking was found,
He brought Kök Keneş into contact,
You became my eyes in the enclosure,
My Talas man, mount up,
If you are still traveling,
My word is counsel and advice,
Old man, that is what I said.
Tie him in the enclosure and lead him out,
I speak words reckoned among tens of thousands,
I speak of my concern to Keneş,
May you never disappear from sight.
My cherished khan Keneş,
Searching as he went, he found him,
What sort of swift steed he was,
He proved to be an ambling horse,
A great encampment for the heroes
Baibaba’s great encampment,
To lay down what was advancing,
To Keneş, who captured horses,
If we are not found for the champion.
If you accept it, O world,
Place the blaze before his eyes,
Kanykei spoke smoothly,
Let us be companions on the journey,
To consent to what she said:
“I am exhausted in mind, my companion,
To become a companion,
Being a warrior from the two Tülük,
Ertai, Kozum, and Keneş,
Give your support at Ay-Salam,
“My eyes burn; give it,” she said,
To send my companion among the people,
The warrior Keneş, against the Kalmyks,
To take him as a companion,”—
Thus Eleseñ spoke.
Keneş had cried out without doing it,
His character seems difficult,
He kept speaking amid hardship.
Then Kontoi, dear Kanek,
A word meant for the cherished elder,
Ertai, Kozum, O friends,
The word that you and your people witnessed,
He pondered without making a commotion,
Running a rope toward the ready one,
He was not greatly satisfied by the heedless one,
He pressed it onto the neck and loaded it,
Eleseñ, Kozum—that is the warrior.
He vanished into the mists
Ebegey and Kozoy, those two heroes
Their eyes wearied across the broad distance
Like a city drawn out in speech
His cry was like a black cauldron
Tall yellow reeds beneath the moon
The path of a truly fired bullet
Their eyes strained toward Kenen
All the figures were shrouded
Toward that deserted sand
The hero Kenen received them
Not knowing what to say
Searching in this manner
They gathered what had been scattered
From Ebegey and Kozoy, the two friends
Who could suppress your courage
Thus spoke Ak Jолтой
Let me put it around his neck
Pleading with the two heroes
Ebegey was overcome
A skin of kumis for the two friends
My eyes across the river
The white hero was taken
Dust rose until the moon came up
I send a thousand troubled greetings
To the poor man’s frozen back
Blood flowed like a black swan
They became those who broke the stake
Ebegey and Kozoy, the two friends
The lash of his weary gaze
Saying that he had given aid
Saying the falcons themselves had come
My uncle Ak Jолтой said this
Babedi made him rich
Driving many sheep and slaughtering them
The raiding host held a roaring feast
Binding many who knew no deceit
Making a final boast his condition
Thus he laid down the condition
While the plain burned with unrest
Brandishing and casting the spear
His messenger sped beyond the wind
He was a youth with people and homeland
What he said was not divided in two
Without haste like the wind
He was a soul who flew like an arrow
A herd was slaughtered in the mountains
It was said the road could not be reached
It was a seven-stranded twist
In the season of the blue loom
Running in this way to the right
When the fierce wind blew
At the middle hour of night
While the people slept
The field guest of forty sons
Where is the good news for Kozoy
To you who stilled the bloodshed
What remained went to the iron fortress
From your courage, to the camp
He brought news to Jолтой
Ebegey and Kozoy, the two friends
They came to give you aid
The bay stallion crossed the open ground
The bronze host formed its enclosure
The distant host moved forth
Gathering all who came out
Wisdom became their companion
Lead your falcons and make camp
Let a road be made through your hardship
Each day he pondered deeply
One in purpose and one in life
Of the hero without Ebegey
Bring the two sides to agreement
Hero, let the needed livestock be ready
Raising his hand at dawn
Slaking thirst from afar
May Khidr remain with you all
Turn back and keep building
Falcon Kozoy, make camp
Make a road for those in distress
If you endure winter, things will mend
Know your lord
If sent among the Kyrgyz, he will not suffer
You two lions like Kobul
You were accepted by both sides
Good fortune came to you
If you wish it, the voice of news has come
What fortune has come as its equal
Ebegey and Kozoy, the two friends
A bold greeting to all of you
The two heroes who heard the news arrived
If you see the custom, know it thus
If Jолтой acts, that is the hero
Let us begin from the news
Let us ease the grieving heart
The day warms and grows glad
If you send him, this is the tiger
Without letting the black shield be struck
Hero, what kind of day is yours today
If you act harshly, he will overturn it
If you wait, let him make camp
If you think firmly, we shall not hurry
May your blessing hold fast
If you wait, that will be your seal
If you receive him for yourself
All of these are heroes
They will grieve when he departs
They will be fulfilled when he comes
He came and heard the question
For the many, rich fortune fills the belly
An inheritance has come to you
If you consider the deed he did
It is a campaign handed down from the ancestors
Know that hero Kenen has come
A khan has come to all of you
The sword-bearing warrior has now arrived
Tomorrow too it will be here
He who proudly establishes the camp
This is the face of paradise
If surrounded, take care
If divided, that is the road
The lord’s true purpose has arrived
That true hero himself was there,
A hero named Tulku came forth,
Who had been held captive,
To all the foremost elders,
The heroes came and met,
Having come and gathered from the beginning,
When the storm-driven wind struck,
